content.text:
Yes, that's right, with three details:

1. **Two ways to run Moneo:**
   - **Not technical:** download the installer from the GitHub Releases page (Windows, Mac or Linux), install it and open it. Nothing else is needed: no Docker, no terminal, no code.
   - **Technical:** download the code and run it with `npm run setup` and `npm run dev`, the same as before.
   - **Phone access through Tailscale works with both.** The downloaded app can also be opened from your phone.

2. **Both use the same code.** A UI change, an AI change or a new page made for the website version also ends up in the app. But app users only get it when you publish a new release and they download and install it again. The app doesn't update itself yet.

3. **Publishing a release is a manual step.** Merging doesn't publish anything. To release:
   - Push a version tag, for example `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.
   - CI then builds all the installers and creates a draft release.
   - You click **Publish** on GitHub.

   The installers aren't code-signed yet. Windows will show a "Windows protected your PC" warning (click More info → Run anyway). On a Mac, the first open needs right-click → Open.

**Merging:** you asked me to merge, so I will, but not yet. GitHub is still blocking it because the checks for the latest commit (the idle-connection fix) are running. I'll merge into `main` as soon as they pass. If any fail, I'll fix that first and won't merge until everything passes.

// Preload for the local setup/status window only (the app window has none). It exposes progress
// updates and four buttons, nothing else; the main process checks every call's sender.
import { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } from "electron";

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("moneoSetup", {
  state: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:state"),
  onState: (callback: (state: unknown) => void) => { ipcRenderer.on("setup:state", (_event, state) => callback(state)); },
  retry: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:retry"),
  openLogs: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:open-logs"),
  restoreBackup: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:restore"),
  quit: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:quit"),
});
{
  "name": "moneo-desktop",
  "productName": "Moneo",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Moneo personal finance, running privately on this computer.",
  "author": "Moneo contributors",
  "homepage": "https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo",
  "license": "MIT",
  "private": true,
  "main": "dist/main.js"

# Builds Moneo Desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux, smoke-tests the packaged app, and on a `v*` tag
# drafts a GitHub release with the installers. Packages are unsigned unless the signing secrets exist.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "scripts/desktop/**"
      - "next.config.ts"
      - "package*.json"
      - "supabase/migrations/**"
      - ".github/workflows/desktop.yml"
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: desktop-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: ${{ matrix.id }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
          name: smoke-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: smoke/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 3

  release:
    name: Draft release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: moneo-desktop-*
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Draft the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version; installer file names carry $version."

            --title "Moneo Desktop $TAG" \
            --notes "Moneo Desktop $TAG. Packages are unsigned unless noted; check SHA256SUMS.txt." \

import { contextBridge, ipcRenderer } from "electron";

contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("moneoSetup", {
  state: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:state"),
  onState: (callback: (state: unknown) => void) => { ipcRenderer.on("setup:state", (_event, state) => callback(state)); },
  retry: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:retry"),
  openLogs: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:open-logs"),
  restoreBackup: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:restore"),
  quit: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("setup:quit"),
});

I'm weighing whether the Settings UI can reach the main process without a preload, since the app window doesn't have one. One option is a Next API route, `/api/desktop/update`, that talks to main over a loopback bridge like the existing auth-return one. I'm also wondering whether a phone request hitting that same route could trigger an update on the computer.

I'm weighing whether a remote phone request to the update route should be allowed to trigger an update on the computer, and I'm thinking of gating it with the existing remote-device check, the same way the logins are handled. For the updater itself, electron-updater looks like the standard choice over a custom one, though I'm checking whether it bundles cleanly with esbuild, since it depends on several libraries and needs the release metadata files and blockmaps that electron-builder generates.

I'm checking the release side next: electron-builder would generate the latest yml files and blockmaps if a publish config is set, and the workflow would need to upload them along with the release being published rather than left as a draft. On Windows, electron-updater only checks signatures if the app is signed, so unsigned builds would rely on the HTTPS download and the sha512 in the metadata file, which is about the same trust as a manual download. On macOS, unsigned builds can't auto-install, so I'm planning to limit automatic installs to Windows and Linux AppImage and send Mac users to the release page instead.

I'm checking whether electron-updater's quit-and-install path works with our before-quit handler, since the installer is spawned before the app quits and our handler calls app.exit. I'm also wondering whether the NSIS installer will wait for the app to close or force it shut, which would affect how cleanly services stop.

I'm working out how the updater would stop services before installing, so the NSIS installer doesn't have to kill postgres mid-shutdown. The plan is to call stopServices first, then quitAndInstall, letting the before-quit handler finish with app.exit.

I'm settling on the update status shape for the main process: idle, checking, available, not-available, downloading with a percent, downloaded, or error, along with the version. The bridge would expose status, check, and install commands, and I'm weighing whether to extend the existing auth-return server rather than add a second one.

I'm settling on the bridge rename: the auth-return server becomes a general bridge with a `startBridge` that takes both the return handler and the update commands, and the Next side gets a matching desktop-bridge module with a connection return and an update action. I'm also checking whether an unpackaged or dev build would make electron-updater skip itself, since win-unpacked reports as packaged but may lack the app-update config.

I'm planning to have the update flow reach the main process through the bridge, and I'm thinking about making the update's download and install steps testable with a feed override, with the existing package-upgrade script as a possible base for an end-to-end check.

I'm planning a verification step that reuses the package-upgrade script: install a first build, serve a second version's feed locally, then trigger check and install to confirm the app relaunches on the new version with data intact. I'm also settling the Settings UI as a conditional "App updates" section with a version display, a check button, and a single "Update now" action that downloads, installs, and restarts.

I'm planning to look at the Settings page structure, the remote-device helper, the package-upgrade script, and whether electron-updater is already in node_modules. I'm also dropping the idea of a settings hint on source checkouts, since I'll just skip the section there.

- name: Fetch the native backend
        run: node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform ${{ matrix.id }}

      - run: npm run desktop:build

      - name: Package

          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          WIN_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_LINK }}
          WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          # Secrets that do not exist arrive as empty strings; unset them so electron-builder
          # treats the build as unsigned.
          for name in CSC_LINK CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID WIN_CSC_LINK WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then unset "$name"; fi
          done
          if [ -z "${CSC_LINK:-}" ] && [ -z "${WIN_CSC_LINK:-}" ]; then

      - name: List packages

content.thinking:
On AppImage, the new instance launches right away, before the old one has quit. Its single-instance lock fails, so it quits, and the old instance's second-instance handler reopens the window while it is shutting down, leaving nothing running afterward. For Linux, I'm considering skipping isForceRunAfter and calling app.relaunch() once services have stopped in quit(), before app.exit.

For AppImage, I'd call quitAndInstall(true, false) with a `relaunchAfterQuit` flag, then in quit() call app.relaunch({ execPath: process.env.APPIMAGE }) before app.exit(0). Plain process.execPath would point into the unmounted squashfs after the mv, so APPIMAGE is the right path to pass. On Windows the installer's --force-run already waits for our app to exit, so it needs no change.

I'm passing a relaunch callback into the updater on Linux so the flag gets set before quitAndInstall triggers the quit. Next I'll set up the update feed for testing, which is only honored in debug builds, and then write updates.ts.

content.content:
Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital).

## Install

### Desktop preview

Desktop installers are being validated for Windows, macOS and Linux; no desktop release has been published yet. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported.
Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed.

### Easiest: let an AI agent install it

If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste:
- Closing the window keeps Moneo in the tray, so background syncs and phone access keep working.
  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it
  to the front; the browser tab says to continue in Moneo. The server reaches the window through a
  loopback address that is random for each launch and refuses browser requests (`src/auth-return.ts`);
  if the window cannot take it, the browser shows the result as in a source checkout. Every other address also goes to the browser
  (https only). The window allows only the microphone and copying, for Moneo's own pages.

### Bank return certificate

6:## Build
12:npm run desktop:dist                     # installers → desktop/release (Windows NSIS, macOS dmg+zip, Linux AppImage+deb)
13:npm run desktop:smoke                    # drive the packaged app (desktop/release/*-unpacked) end to end
